chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, from Ibn Mayyah, from Yunus, from the one who informed him, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:
When you comb your head and your beard, then wipe the comb upon your chest, for it removes the worry and the illness (fever).
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of combing the beard according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* from Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him), this hadith links physical grooming with spiritual and physiological well-being, suggesting that the simple act of combing the head and beard while touching the chest serves as a means to alleviate anxiety (*hamm*) and ward off illness (*wabā'*). This practice reflects the Shia tradition of finding barakah (blessing) in daily routines, transforming mundane hygiene into a ritual of mental and physical purification.
